message.content:
The two unknowns \(x\) (length) and \(y\) (width) satisfy  

\[
\begin{cases}
2(x+y)=14 \quad &(\text{perimeter})\\[4pt]
xy=15          \quad &(\text{area})
\end{cases}\Longrightarrow 
\begin{cases}
x+y=7 \\[4pt]
xy=15 .
\end{cases}
\]

Eliminate one variable using the first equation:
\(y = 7-x\).  
Substitute into the second:

\[
x(7-x)=15 \;\Rightarrow\;
7x - x^{2}=15 \;\Rightarrow\;
x^{2}-7x+15=0 .
\]

This quadratic has discriminant  

\[
\Delta = (-7)^2-4\cdot1\cdot15 = 49-60 = -\,11<0 .
\]

A negative discriminant means **no real‑valued solutions** exist – it’s mathematically impossible for a rectangle to have both a perimeter of 14 units *and* an area of 15 square units simultaneously.

If you were willing to accept complex side lengths, the solutions would be

\[
x=\frac{7\pm i\sqrt{11}}{2}, \qquad
y=\frac{7\mp i\sqrt{11}}{2},
\]

but physically this does not correspond to a real rectangle. Thus, under ordinary geometric assumptions, **there is no rectangle satisfying those conditions.**
